hook: A red giant orbits an unseen object that may be a supermassive neutron star or a light black hole.
summary: A red giant in a wide, low-eccentricity orbit has an invisible companion whose mass falls in the gap between neutron stars and black holes. Radial velocities and Gaia astrometry gave the orbit, and no light from a second star was found in infrared spectra. The mass depends on an uncertain inclination, and the companion is not directly seen.
title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary.
